argument: Modern cryptography defines security through games: no adversary within a resource class should distinguish, forge, learn, or bias more than a negligible amount. Proofs reduce a successful attack to breaking an assumed-hard primitive.
boundary: Security is conditional on adversary model, implementation, key management, randomness, and hardness assumptions.
Side channels and social attacks can bypass a sound reduction.
Quantum adversaries change which assumptions remain credible.
claim: Modern cryptography defines security through games: no adversary within a resource class should distinguish, forge, learn, or bias more than a negligible amount. Proofs reduce a successful attack to breaking an assumed-hard primitive.
interpretation: Never label a system simply “secure.” Store the security notion, adversary powers, reduction, and implementation boundary.
